standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-finiteness gives finiteness of the induced fraction field extension
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at the start of the counted proof (lines 45425-45429)

standard_prerequisites.name: The integral closure as a finite module over an N-2 base
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used in the middle of the counted proof (lines 45430-45446)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces a finite intermediate ring whose integral closure over the target is the object whose finiteness has to be shown.

core_obligations: Note that the induced fraction field extension is finite and use the N-2 property of the base to obtain finiteness statements for the integral closure of an intermediate ring (proof lines 45424-45440).

Choose the intermediate ring so that the target is obtained from it without changing the fraction field, and conclude finiteness of the integral closure of the target by transitivity of integral closure and permanence of finiteness (proof lines 45440-45448).
proof_roadmap: Apply the N-2 property of the base to the finite field extension (proof lines 45424-45440).
Move to an intermediate ring and finish by transitivity (proof lines 45440-45449).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a quasi-finite extension of domains over a Noetherian N-2 base is again N-2 (statement lines 45418-45422). The proof does not argue with the definition of quasi-finiteness directly: it notes that the induced fraction field extension is finite, applies the N-2 property of the base to it, passes to a suitable intermediate ring where finiteness of the integral closure can be transferred, and finishes using transitivity of integral closure and permanence of finiteness (proof lines 45424-45449). Choosing the intermediate ring so that the transfer applies is the content. H2.
